question: Which hormone is the main one responsible for lowering your blood sugar after you eat a meal?
explanation: Spot on! Insulin is released by your pancreas to help glucose move out of your bloodstream and into your body cells to give you energy. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h1)

question: Why do doctors prescribe antidiabetic medications for patients with diabetes mellitus?

options.A: To restore normal metabolic balance and lower blood sugar
options.B: To permanently replace the need for dietary modifications
options.C: To stimulate the continuous release of stored glucagon
options.D: To completely cure the underlying pancreatic disease

explanation: You got it! These drugs help keep blood glucose in check to prevent long-term complications, even though they aren't a permanent cure on their own. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h1)

question: Why must insulin be given as an injection instead of swallowing it as a pill?

options.A: Injections allow insulin to bypass the liver entirely
options.B: Digestive enzymes in the stomach destroy the insulin molecule
options.C: Stomach acid turns insulin into a toxic compound
options.D: Oral pills are absorbed too rapidly to be safe

explanation: Exactly! Insulin is a protein, so the acids and enzymes in your gut would break it down before it ever reached your bloodstream if you swallowed it. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h2)

question: What is the main difference in how drug treatment is chosen for type 1 versus type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Type 1 is managed strictly through lifestyle changes without drugs
options.B: Type 2 patients never need insulin under any clinical circumstances
options.C: Type 2 can only be treated with injectable non-insulin medications
options.D: Type 1 always requires insulin, while type 2 often starts with oral agents

explanation: Well done! Because type 1 diabetes means the body doesn't make insulin at all, replacement therapy is needed right from the start. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h2)

question: About how fast does rapid-acting insulin start working after you inject it?
explanation: Spot on! Rapid-acting insulin starts working almost immediately, which is why patients need to have their food ready right away. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h3)

question: A patient just took a morning injection of regular (short-acting) insulin. When should the nurse watch out for the highest risk of low blood sugar?

options.A: Twelve to twenty-four hours after injection
options.B: Two to three hours after injection

explanation: You got it! Short-acting insulin usually peaks around 2 to 3 hours, meaning that's when blood sugar drops the fastest and needs close monitoring. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h3)

question: What is the main way Metformin helps lower blood sugar in the body?

options.A: Stimulating the beta cells of the pancreas to release stored insulin
options.B: Slowing down the digestion of carbohydrates in the small intestine
options.C: Decreasing hepatic glucose production and improving insulin sensitivity
options.D: Blocking the reabsorption of glucose in the renal tubules

explanation: Exactly right! Metformin tells the liver to ease up on making extra sugar and helps your body's cells respond better to your natural insulin. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h4)

question: Why do sulfonylurea drugs carry a higher risk of causing low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia) compared to Metformin?

options.A: They destroy counter-regulatory hormones like glucagon and cortisol
options.B: They force the kidneys to dump excess sugar into the urine too quickly
options.C: They actively stimulate insulin release from the pancreas regardless of blood sugar levels
options.D: They completely block the liver from releasing any stored glucose ever

explanation: Spot on! Sulfonylureas keep pushing the pancreas to pump out insulin even if blood sugar levels are already dropping, which can cause hypoglycaemia. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h4)

question: How do SGLT2 inhibitor medications help lower your blood glucose?

options.A: By increasing the sensitivity of muscle receptors to circulating insulin
options.B: By stopping the liver from producing any new glucose molecules
options.C: By blocking renal glucose reabsorption and causing excretion in urine
options.D: By stimulating the pancreas to release extra insulin after meals

explanation: You nailed it! These drugs stop your kidneys from reabsorbing filtered sugar, so the extra glucose simply passes out through your urine. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h5)

question: What common side effect should you warn a patient about when they start taking an SGLT2 inhibitor?

options.A: Severe low blood sugar episodes occurring mostly during the night
options.B: Genital fungal infections due to increased glucose in the urine
options.C: Permanent kidney failure caused by excessive strain on the nephrons
options.D: Rapid and dangerous weight gain from fluid retention in the legs

explanation: Well done! Since there is extra sugar in the urine, it creates a sweet environment where fungi love to grow, increasing the risk of local infections. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h5)

question: What blood glucose level is generally used to define hypoglycaemia (low blood sugar) in clinical practice?
explanation: Spot on! Any reading under 3.9 mmol/L (70 mg/dL) means the blood sugar is too low and the patient needs help quickly. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h6)

question: A patient taking gliclazide is awake but looks shaky, sweaty, and confused. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Wait patiently for thirty minutes to see if symptoms pass
options.B: Inject a large dose of long-acting insulin subcutaneously
options.C: Administer 15 grams of fast-acting oral carbohydrates
options.D: Encourage the patient to go for a brisk walk to burn energy

explanation: You got it! Giving quick sugar (like juice or a glucose tablet) safely raises their blood sugar and fixes those scary early symptoms fast. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h6)

question: Why is it important for nurses in Nigeria to ask patients about any traditional herbal remedies they might be taking?

options.A: Traditional herbs are scientifically proven to cure type 1 diabetes permanently
options.B: Herbal products completely replace the need for blood glucose monitoring
options.C: Traditional remedies have no chemical impact on human liver enzymes
options.D: Herbal mixtures can interact with prescribed drugs and cause unexpected blood sugar drops

explanation: Spot on! Many local herbal preparations can unexpectedly drop blood sugar levels, leading to severe hypoglycaemia when mixed with regular diabetes medications. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h7)

question: A patient with type 1 diabetes lives somewhere without reliable electricity and asks how to keep their insulin cool. What is a helpful, practical suggestion?

options.A: Use a clay pot evaporative cooler system to store the insulin safely
options.B: Keep the insulin bottle in direct sunlight to keep it warm and dry
options.C: Store the insulin inside the family cooking pot near the fireplace
options.D: Leave the insulin exposed on the open windowsill during the night

explanation: Brilliant! A clay pot cooler (pot-in-pot evaporative cooling) is a fantastic, traditional way to lower storage temperatures without needing a fridge or electricity. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h7)
